held_out_title: You asked me to roast your AI resumes.. so I did.

config.corpus_note: 3 of 53 videos have no stored summary, so the summary-filtered setup routes over 50 videos before the held-out one is removed

matches.criterion: A resume should fit on a single page, even for an engineer with more than ten years of experience.
matches.quote: you want to keep your resume to just a single page
matches.note: Page count is a resume mechanic; a scrolling website has no equivalent.

matches.criterion: Cut or reorder experience that is irrelevant to the role being targeted, instead of listing everything you have ever done.
matches.quote: shuffle your experience around to make it make the most sense for the job application

matches.criterion: Work should show clear individual ownership of what was built, not merely participation in a team that built it.
matches.quote: there's clear ownership of the projects. It's not just about building something with a team

matches.criterion: Keep the opening summary to two or three lines and do not restate there what the body of the document already proves.
matches.quote: reduce their professional summary to just two to three lines

matches.criterion: Put explicit numbers on claims of scale or reliability rather than leaving the reader to take the claim on trust.
matches.quote: be a little bit more explicit about how many releases there actually were
matches.finding_criterion: Quantify achievements with metrics and data to show impact.

matches.criterion: There must be a visible career narrative that leads from the previous roles into the role now being applied for.
matches.quote: there is no clear story that leads this person into AI engineering

matches.criterion: Build one flagship project in the target domain that bridges the existing professional experience to the job being sought.
matches.quote: they don't have their own North Star project to showcase in the resume, there isn't a clear bridge

matches.criterion: Limit any one role to about three bullet points, however long that role lasted.
matches.quote: limit the bullet points here to a maximum of three
matches.note: About the bullet list under an employment entry, which a project portfolio does not have.

matches.criterion: Compress older roles to one or two lines rather than removing them, so the years of experience still show without consuming space.
matches.quote: you can optimize one or two lines in each of these sections and just keep them brief

matches.criterion: Drop courses and credentials that add nothing for the target role, because the skill should be evident from the work instead.
matches.quote: I don't know what the added value is of this online course on training great tech leaders
matches.finding_criterion: Favor substantial independent projects over generic or required coursework.

matches.criterion: Do not carry a separate skills list that repeats what the described work already demonstrates.
matches.quote: remove the skill section altogether because your skills will be very obvious from the work experience itself

matches.criterion: Include links to your profiles and code so a reader can independently check that the projects are real.
matches.quote: links to LinkedIn, GitHub and actually a way to check out the validity of the projects mentioned
matches.finding_criterion: Make it easy for a recruiter to learn more by embedding links to LinkedIn, a personal website, GitHub, and blog posts/case studies.

matches.criterion: Cut vague competence claims that could be said of anyone in the role and that the employment history already implies.
matches.quote: these kinds of fluffy sentences are really just a waste of the potential recruiter's attention

matches.criterion: A recruiter gives the document twenty to thirty seconds, so the most convincing material has to be reachable immediately.
matches.quote: You really want to make sure that they get to the meat of your resume as soon as possible

matches.criterion: Order the document so the strongest project sits at the very top, above any list of technologies.
matches.quote: put your top project, your North Star project, at the very top

matches.criterion: Describe a project concretely enough that the underlying skills are self-evident, instead of asserting the skills separately.
matches.quote: skills like being able to build scalable solutions will be obvious from the project description alone
matches.finding_criterion: Present skills as concrete tools and applications rather than abstract knowledge areas.

matches.criterion: Check the document for stale statements left over from an earlier version, such as naming the wrong target role.
matches.quote: I assume that this is kind of from a previous version of the resume, but double-check these kinds of things

matches.criterion: Keep the document in a plain-text source format such as LaTeX or markdown so it can be machine-checked before each application.
matches.quote: resume should be written in a format like LaTeX or a markdown file
matches.note: A reviewer of a published site sees only the rendered output, so there is no source document for them to judge. (The earlier reason given here — that a website has no plain-text source — was simply wrong for a GitHub Pages site.)

matches.criterion: Reframe the earlier career as the foundation the target-domain work is built on, rather than as unrelated prior history.
matches.quote: reframed where the data infrastructure fundamentals that this person has is a foundation for the AI pipelines

matches.criterion: Keep the education section to a single line once you have been working for years.
matches.quote: the education section is very slim here. It's just a single line
matches.note: The portfolio has no education section to keep to a line.

matches.criterion: Put certifications inside the experience they apply to and deep-link the proof, instead of listing them on their own line.
matches.quote: add a deep link to a certification platform where it shows the proof that you got that certification
matches.note: About where certifications sit inside an employment history; the portfolio lists no certifications.

matches.criterion: Aim the whole document at one clear role persona and build everything else around it.
matches.quote: You want to aim for one clear role persona and build the rest of your resume around that
matches.finding_criterion: Tailor the portfolio to the specific target role instead of using one generic resume for every job.

matches.criterion: Cut corporate jargon and reduce the volume of prose, because too much text crowds out the actual evidence.
matches.quote: there's a lot of corporate jargon because essentially we are trained to use corporate jargon

matches.criterion: Every project mentioned should carry a link to the artifact itself so a reader can verify it exists.
matches.quote: none of them have an embedded link to a GitHub page

findings.criterion: Quantify achievements with metrics and data to show impact.
findings.detail: The portfolio leads with 'I build agents and prove they work' and gives a number for almost every project: '9/9 red-team attacks stopped at the guardrail gate', '77.1% eval-verified accuracy', '10,250 predictions scored', and '6.1× fewer tokens at 0.93 answer parity'.

citations.quote: quantify your contributions by using metrics and data to Showcase your impact

citation_checks.quote: quantify your contributions by using metrics and data to Showcase your impact

findings.criterion: Only link to live, working, current portfolio sites, GitHub repos, and project pages.
findings.detail: The supplied site is itself a GitHub Pages URL and the page links to GitHub, LinkedIn, and per-project case studies rather than to obviously dead or placeholder links.

citations.quote: if you have any links to anything that might be live like a GitHub repo or the actual website that you worked on that is a huge bonus point if it looks really bad or it doesn't work or it's outdated which I've seen on a lot of the resumes I got today please do not include it
never link a a dead GitHub and never link a bad portfolio site make sure if you link something it is updated and it looks good

citation_checks.quote: if you have any links to anything that might be live like a GitHub repo or the actual website that you worked on that is a huge bonus point if it looks really bad or it doesn't work or it's outdated which I've seen on a lot of the resumes I got today please do not include it
never link a a dead GitHub and never link a bad portfolio site make sure if you link something it is updated and it looks good

findings.criterion: Make it easy for a recruiter to learn more by embedding links to LinkedIn, a personal website, GitHub, and blog posts/case studies.
findings.detail: The header and footer include GitHub and LinkedIn links and a 'Contact on LinkedIn ↗' link, and every project has a 'Case study →' link, so a reviewer can click through for more detail.

citations.quote: provide and embed links to Linkin ideally even a personal website blog posts and more

citation_checks.quote: provide and embed links to Linkin ideally even a personal website blog posts and more

findings.criterion: Keep formatting clean, consistent, and free of typos and messy alignment.
findings.detail: The page uses a consistent dark/light layout, clear section headings, and the provided text appears free of typos and visible alignment issues.

citations.quote: formatting is very important. So avoid the messy alignment, random fund sizes, grammatical mistakes. These are small things but they scream unprofessional

citation_checks.quote: formatting is very important. So avoid the messy alignment, random fund sizes, grammatical mistakes. These are small things but they scream unprofessional

findings.criterion: Include your location so recruiters can screen for geography without extra clicks.
findings.detail: This portfolio does not show a city, state, country, or any location; a recruiter would have to click through to LinkedIn to find it.

citations.quote: his location this is one of the most important things a recruiter is going to look for in your application sure you probably input it when you're applying to the job but having that on your resume is also very important

citation_checks.quote: his location this is one of the most important things a recruiter is going to look for in your application sure you probably input it when you're applying to the job but having that on your resume is also very important

findings.criterion: Present skills as concrete tools and applications rather than abstract knowledge areas.
findings.detail: The opening line says 'agentic systems, RAG pipelines and the eval harnesses' — these are application areas more than tools — but specific technologies such as AWS App Runner, Slack, D3, sha256 manifests, and GAN do appear in the project descriptions, so the page mostly grounds the skills in real tools.

citations.quote: skill is not equal to subject. In your skill section in resume don't write things like machine learning or statistics under skills that is knowledge not a skill. Write how you apply that knowledge.

citation_checks.quote: skill is not equal to subject. In your skill section in resume don't write things like machine learning or statistics under skills that is knowledge not a skill. Write how you apply that knowledge.

findings.criterion: Explain each project like a product with problem, approach, and lessons, not just a code dump.
findings.detail: Each project block is paired with a 'Case study →' link and a headline metric, which points reviewers toward a fuller problem/solution write-up rather than leaving them to read code.

citations.quote: Every project should have a one-page report or drive PDF link in your resume which should have what problem did you solve in this project, what text you used, what challenges did you face and what did you learn from those challenges.

citation_checks.quote: Every project should have a one-page report or drive PDF link in your resume which should have what problem did you solve in this project, what text you used, what challenges did you face and what did you learn from those challenges.

findings.criterion: Tailor the portfolio to the specific target role instead of using one generic resume for every job.
findings.detail: The site is clearly focused on Applied AI Engineering: the title, the tagline, and the 'Selected systems' section all feature agents, RAG, evals, and governed data work, with no unrelated projects competing for attention.

citations.quote: Different roles having different stories. I have seen people applying for data scientist, ML engineer, AI engineer all with the same resume. That is the biggest mistake. Customize it.

citation_checks.quote: Different roles having different stories. I have seen people applying for data scientist, ML engineer, AI engineer all with the same resume. That is the biggest mistake. Customize it.

findings.criterion: Favor substantial independent projects over generic or required coursework.
findings.detail: The featured projects are named systems with concrete metrics, such as V2V Prod Agent, Data Pilot, CUAD Legal Agent, and ConvFinQA Agent, rather than the kind of every-student coursework the experts warn against.

citations.quote: if I see you just listing every single school project it's almost more of a red flag than anything else
